paper.title: Towards Certificate-Driven Software Porting: A Self-Improving Agentic Harness for Scientific Program Optimization
paper.available: Paper HTML/PDF/TeX; no implementation repository linked in the inspected manuscript.
paper.finding: Failed-candidate evidence becomes validated restrictions enforced by code, with compatible edits retained. This is a GPU-porting study, not an ACC search result or whole-program equivalence proof.
paper.relevance: Our negative-memory closure and the observed crash-as-miss failure: a failure record must support exactly the restriction it creates.
paper.bounded_next_experiment: Offline, feed one completed finite miss, one SIGILL record, one timeout, and one changed-input job into an isolated closure-gate fixture. Only the completed unchanged finite scope may suppress that job. Bound 180 seconds/1024 MiB/600000 records; no search keys reopened or production checkpoint changed.

repository.message:
Lineage-diverse beam (--lincap/--linper), cloud-side path polishing, outlier diagnostics

- acs: cap slots per lineage per beam level so one route family cannot take the whole beam
- focus loop + cloud workers rotate two lineage-cap settings
- cloud workers polish our best paths (rebeam + window) every 3rd pass
- check.py skips lines garbled by interrupted writes
- experiment log: outlier diagnostic, relaxation ablation, lineage-cap results

repository.available: Commit tree includes C++ solver, Python training/evaluation code and draft proof-track data; README says competition solution paths are intentionally withheld.
repository.limits: Already reported by UPGH, so not a new lead. Published build defaults use -march=native and describe about 3 GB RAM for ball16, outside this harness's permitted resource profile. No external code downloaded or run, and none imported into harness.
